text:
Maya Patel: quick thread — ran the SSE vs polling vs websocket throughput/latency sweep across regions and GPUs this morning. goal: pick default endpoint for low-latency interactive use and sizing guidance for Dedicated pools.

Ethan Chu: nice. which model and quantization?

Maya Patel: llama2-13b v2, FP16 and 4-bit (nf4) quant. kernels: flash-attn (torch), cutlass-optimized for H100, and a fallback cuBLAS transformer path. sequences were typical chat (avg prompt+gen = 512 tokens).

Priya Rao: what traffic pattern? steady vs burst?

Maya Patel: two patterns: steady 50 concurrent users with 1 rps each (long tail think chat), and bursty 500 concurrent for 10s every 5min to simulate PLG spikes. measured p50/p95/p99 latency and sustained throughput (tokens/s and reqs/s).

perf-bot: perf summary uploaded: https://internal.redwood/perf/1914202023 — check the raw CSVs.

Maya Patel: pasted the condensed results below (p50,p95,p99 in ms for token streaming vs classical non-streaming HTTP completion; throughput in reqs/s under given concurrency).

```
Region,GPU,Endpoint,Mode,Concurrency,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,reqs_s
us-west1,A100,SSE,streaming,50,80,140,230,420
us-west1,A100,HTTP,non-stream,50,120,260,480,380
us-west1,A100,WS,streaming,50,85,150,240,430
eu-west1,H100,SSE,streaming,50,65,110,190,520
eu-west1,H100,HTTP,non-stream,50,100,200,370,460
eu-west1,H100,WS,streaming,50,70,115,200,510
us-west1,A100,SSE,streaming,500(burst),250,480,820,1200
us-west1,A100,HTTP,non-stream,500(burst),520,980,1600,900
us-west1,A100,WS,streaming,500(burst),260,500,850,1180
```

Maya Patel: takeaways: streaming (SSE/WS) consistently gives lower p50/p95 for interactive workloads; SSE slightly ahead of WS in our infra due to HTTP/2 multiplexing overhead differences. Under heavy burst, SSE+batching with KV cache saved ~15% tokens, improving effective throughput. H100 shows better steady throughput per-device but requires different cutlass kernels to hit p99 targets.

Ethan Chu: interesting — H100 had better reqs/s but lower p99 headroom? can you share the kernel breakdown metric?

Maya Patel: yep — kernel breakdown: flash-attn path reduced attention kernel latency by ~30% on A100 for sequences <768. On H100, cutlass 8-bit matmul + optimized attention reduced token latency but increased variability for long sequences; p99 spikes came from fallback paths and NVLink saturation in eu-west1 during bursts.

Priya Rao: any config knobs that helped? autotune batch/window?

Maya Patel: tuned batching window to 30ms for SSE which balanced latency and throughput for 50 conc. For bursts we increased max batch size and enabled aggressive prefix KV caching. Also set routing policy: prefer H100 for steady, fallback to A100 when busy.

Jonas Klein: question for Dedicated sizing: with 500 concurrent burst, what’s the recommended GPU pool size for 99% of bursts without fallbacks?

Maya Patel: ballpark: for us-west1 with A100, 6x A100 nodes per 500 concurrent (given our batch profile and quant4). For H100 in eu-west1, 4x H100 nodes. These assume we keep SSE streaming and batching windows at 30ms and KV caching enabled.

Ethan Chu: any quality regression from 4-bit vs fp16 in streaming? we care about hallucination/score drops.

Maya Patel: small regen test on eval set: perplexity increased ~2.1% and ROUGE-L delta ~ -0.6 on our chat eval — within acceptable alert thresholds. We flagged a few prompts where decoding shifts were visible; will add to the eval suite.

perf-bot: perf alerts: none triggered.

Priya Rao: can we surface a quick chart in Console per-route showing p95 vs throughput for SSE vs HTTP? that’d help PMs choose defaults.

Maya Patel: agreed — I'll upload a two-panel chart (SSE vs HTTP) and a recommended config snippet. snippet below for reference: 

```
route: /v1/chat
endpoint: streaming_sse
batching:
  max_window_ms: 30
  max_batch_size: 64
caching:
  kv_prefix: true
quant: nf4
fallbacks:
  - model_variant: llama2-13b-fp16
    region_priority: [us-west1, eu-west1]
```

Jonas Klein: thanks — if you can add the H100 kernel tags to the console we can auto-select cutlass for eu-west1.

Maya Patel: will do, adding tickets for eng-runtime to wire kernel hints to routing.

Ethan Chu: can you attach the raw p99 tail traces for one burst window? want to see NVLink saturation.

Maya Patel: attached in perf link. TL;DR: NVLink/PCIe stalls + GC pause on one worker node correlated with the p99 spike. mitigation: stagger worker GC and increase host buf pool.

Priya Rao: perfect. next step: prod canary switching default for interactive routes to SSE in us-west1 with H100 preference. i'll draft rollout plan. :+1:
